steps.title: Find the client's documents (three routes), register them, name the insurer behind each
do: Find the documents the page below lists in the client's own folders. Try the routes IN THIS ORDER and record EVERY try, failures too:
1  device: the computer (local drive / OneDrive)    2  m365: the Microsoft 365 connector    3  zapier: the Zapier Office 365 tools
Record each try: python3 {scripts}/run.py access {run} --purpose locate --route device|m365|zapier --result failed|found --note "what you did"

Register each quote or in-force schedule (one per policy or proposal; the label is its own name, for example the insurer and product): python3 {scripts}/run.py doc {run} --role quote|schedule --label "Label" --file <local copy> --route <the route>

Register the intake documents: the Follow-Up Appointment Summary Notes (every dated version, --role intake_notes --label "<date>"), the Fact Find Summary (--role fact_find_summary) and the WR Overview (--role overview), from the client's `2. Fact Find` folder first, then the main folder.
Declare the insurer behind each quote or schedule: python3 {scripts}/run.py insurers {run} --file insurers.json
Every intake document is registered or confirmed not to exist with Paul's words (`--missing`). A quote or schedule can never be missing: STOP and ask Paul.
Show Paul the 'what I found' list (one line per document: file name, date, folder, and anything missing, conflicting or unreadable, such as a RAR where a schedule should be) in your reply.
steps.proof: the tries are logged in order, two or more quotes or schedules are registered, the intake documents are registered or accounted for, every insurer is declared

steps.title: Read the registered documents, one page at a time
do: Run: python3 {scripts}/run.py read {run}

The program shows the text page by page. Read each page fully, then acknowledge it with a one-line note (`run.py read {run} --ack KEY:PAGE --note "..."`). Pages are acknowledged in order; a page with no readable text must be viewed as an image by you.
steps.proof: every page was served in order and acknowledged

steps.title: Settle the client's benefit scope from their own notes, the second life, the basis, the voice and the sections
do: Run: python3 {scripts}/run.py scope {run}   (it prints the lines of the notes that mention each benefit category)

Write scope.json in the layout the page below describes, every category with a verbatim line of the notes as evidence (or Paul's own words), then run: python3 {scripts}/run.py scope {run} --file scope.json

Ask Paul ONLY for what the file cannot give: the notes are silent or conflict on a category, the basis (like-for-like or against the proposal) is not recorded, or he wants other sections or the third-person voice.
steps.proof: every category has a line of the client's own notes (or Paul's words) as evidence and the line is in the notes' text

steps.title: Fetch and save each insurer's own guide
do: For EACH declared insurer fetch its own technical guide, product guide or policy wording from the web (the search and fetch tools first, then Claude in Chrome; log every try with --purpose research), SAVE the text in a file and register it.
The program printed the exact commands when you declared the insurers. A guide that cannot be found: ask Paul, then `run.py doc --missing guide --label "<Insurer>" --said "Paul's words"`.
Read each guide page by page like the other documents: python3 {scripts}/run.py read {run}
steps.proof: every insurer has its guide (or Paul's words), each with its web address and date, routes in order, read page by page

steps.title: Enter the figures and statements, each with its evidence; the program checks every one against the documents
do: Write ONE answers file in the layout the page below describes, every figure with a verbatim line of its document, then run: python3 {scripts}/run.py answers {run} --file <your answers file>

The program refuses a figure whose evidence line is not in the document's text or not in the line, a category that is out of scope, a statement with no source, a 'wins' badge on an inference, an 'exclusive' claim not checked against every other insurer, a text over its word limit, a slip of voice, a placeholder, a conflict.
Never type a figure from memory and never copy one from another client. If a figure is missing from the documents, say so; do not research a substitute.
steps.proof: the answers are valid, sourced, and every figure was found in the evidence line it cites

steps.title: The program works out the premium escalation and raises the flags
do: Run: python3 {scripts}/run.py check {run}
Read what it prints. Nothing is typed or adjusted by you. A flag is for Paul: it goes on the confirmation table.
steps.proof: the escalation was worked out by the program from these answers

steps.title: Show Paul the confirmation table, ask ONE question, record his yes
do: Run: python3 {scripts}/run.py show {run}

Put the whole table it prints in your reply (it includes the scope with its evidence, the flags, the statements, the banner and the Verdict, the email subject and the exact Teams message to Sitamah) and ask exactly the one question it gives. Nothing is built before his clear yes.
When he says yes, record his own words: python3 {scripts}/run.py approve {run} --said "his exact words"
If an answer changes, run answers and check again and show again: the earlier yes then no longer counts.
steps.proof: Paul was shown exactly these answers and results and said yes

steps.title: The program draws the letter from the fixed template and builds the email body
do: Run: python3 {scripts}/run.py build {run}
It builds the letter and the email body from your confirmed answers (never typed), checks them, and names the files. You never edit a script, the template or the HTML.
Send the letter to Paul in the chat as a file with the exact file name the program gives.
steps.proof: the files are exactly what the program builds from the confirmed answers and pass the program's checks

steps.title: Save the letter in the client's Comparative Quotes folder, never overwriting without Paul's yes
do: List the client's folder for the risk transaction > `Comparative Quotes` (it can sit one level deeper than the first folder with that name; computer first, then Microsoft 365, then Zapier; record every try with --purpose save) and note the file names already there. Then: python3 {scripts}/run.py name {run} --existing "name one.html;name two.html"
If a file with the same name exists the program stops: ask Paul; only with his yes run it again with --overwrite-yes "his words".
Save exactly the file it names. If the folder does not exist, ask Paul. List the folder again and record what it shows:
python3 {scripts}/run.py receipt {run} save.folder <the folder path>   save.listed_bytes <the html's size in the listing>
steps.proof: the derived name was used, nothing was overwritten without Paul's yes, the folder is Comparative Quotes and the listed size equals the local file

steps.title: Make the Outlook draft with the Microsoft 365 draft tool (never sent by Claude) and read it back for the program
do: Follow the page below. The body to use is the draft_body.html the program built. Read the saved draft back, save the read-back to a file and run: python3 {scripts}/run.py draft {run} --file <the saved read-back>
Every line must be a green tick. Then record: run.py receipt {run} draft.created_with outlook_create_draft
steps.proof: the saved read-back of the draft passes every program check

steps.title: Message Sitamah on Teams through Zapier (the wording is the program's) and read the posted message back
do: Look in the 1:1 chat for whether the same time-of-day greeting was already used today by Paul or Claude, then run: python3 {scripts}/run.py message {run} --used-today yes|no

Send exactly the message it prints, as it says. Read the posted message back, save it to a file, record the receipts it names and run: python3 {scripts}/run.py messagecheck {run} --file <the saved read-back>
steps.proof: the message went to the 1:1 chat as markdown and its read-back passes every program check

steps.title: The final check and the SHORT AUDIT for Paul
do: Run: python3 {scripts}/run.py done {run} final
Put in your reply, as it is: where the letter was saved, the draft's status and who attaches the letter, that Sitamah was messaged, then the short audit. Nothing longer.
Any red cross means the job is not finished: say so.
steps.proof: the final checker prints no red cross
